solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cross artist follows sound of something ringing

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so the second piece is placed behind the first

blocks.note: a chime is the sound a bell makes
RA stands for Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: An irritated painter comes along after hearing a bell or phone ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, describing the artist, but it is the definition, used as a noun meaning a hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a mythical beast built from lion, goat and serpent parts, so a mixed breed or hybrid creature.

clue.text: Clergy member in uniform stopping old banger?

indicators.note: something stopping a gap plugs it, sitting inside the other piece

blocks.note: a crate is slang for a decrepit old car
U is Uniform in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A vicar in uniform is shown standing in the way of a clapped-out car.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a banger is a sausage or a decrepit old car; the question mark admits that CRATE is the slang for the car sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant priest in a Church of England parish, one rank of the clergy.

clue.text: Start wearing silly tango suit outside of theatre

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so the letters are jumbled
the outside of a word is its two end letters, with the middle discarded

blocks.note: dressed in something is wearing it
T is Tango in the phonetic alphabet
taken as written
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A dancer begins a performance dressed in a ridiculous tango costume outside the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like a noun but is the verb definition; 'silly' reworks the T of tango together with SUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute proceedings or a policy is to set them up or begin them, a formal synonym for initiating.

clue.text: Scoundrel leaving with frame from studio?

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so those letters drop out of the word

blocks.note: a weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person
W is a standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A crook makes off from an artist's studio clutching a picture frame.
explanation.walkthrough: Take W from WEASEL. The question mark flags that 'frame' is a stand, not a picture border.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the wooden stand that holds a canvas while a painter works, a fixture of any studio.

clue.text: Adult group that nearly lost sign

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut
lost suggests disoriented and astray, so these letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: A is the film classification for adult
taken as written
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: A grown-ups' club has nearly mislaid its signpost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' at the end reads as a noun lost by the group, but it is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To autograph something is to write one's signature on it, as a celebrity does for fans.

clue.text: Sauce and chocs a bather carries to port

indicators.note: what carries something holds it inside, so the word sits within the run of letters
port is the left side of a ship, so in an across clue the letters travel leftwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A swimmer carts hot sauce and chocolates down to the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' sounds like a harbour or a wine, but sailors use it for the left side, so read the letters right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a brand of fiery chilli pepper sauce from Louisiana, a trademark used generically.

clue.text: Half of story on rubbish picture card

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word keeps two letters and throws the rest away
in a down clue one thing on another sits above it, so the first piece comes first

blocks.note: a story is a tale; its first half
rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: Half a story is written on a trashy picture postcard.
explanation.walkthrough: Story must first become TALE before it is halved.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot cards carry symbolic illustrations and are used for fortune-telling, so each is an illustrated playing card.

clue.text: Louder girl regularly cramped by singer’s musical style

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept
something cramped by another is squeezed inside its walls

blocks.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice
first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A girl singing more loudly feels cramped by the singer's style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Louder' wants to be the musical f or forte, but it is only half of the run of letters being thinned.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluegrass is a genre of American country music from Kentucky, played on banjo, fiddle and mandolin.

clue.text: What an actor might steal is spotted in auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so we go by what is heard

blocks.note: spotted means noticed

explanation.surface: Something an actor pinches is noticed by the audience in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steal' suggests a theft spotted by the audience; the definition is the idiom of upstaging.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who steals the scene draws all attention from fellow performers, so the idiom gives the stolen thing.

clue.text: Best degree held by eccentric tutors

indicators.note: eccentric means odd and irregular, so the letters lose their normal order
what is held by something is gripped inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: The top qualification is earned under odd academic supervisors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' reads as an adjective praising the degree, but it is a verb meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to get the better of them, and to outsmart is to win by cleverness.

clue.text: Game opponents with spades in tricks

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
South and East sit on opposing sides at bridge
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A card game in which rivals holding spades win the tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play East-West, so any two adjacent compass points are opponents. 'tricks' sounds like card play but means deceptions.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a cunning stratagem meant to deceive, so the plural matches deceptive tricks.

clue.text: Wild savage briefly retreated back to bayou fast

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short by its final letter
to retreat is to go backwards, so the letters run the other way
the back of a word is its very last letter

blocks.note: a brute, without its final letter
its last letter
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A wild savage quickly beat a hasty retreat back to the swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' is the noun, a period of fasting, rather than speedy. A bayou is a marshy creek in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent means disorderly and violently agitated, like wild weather or an unruly crowd.

clue.text: Lamp on rear area poorly installed by drunk

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside, so it goes within the other piece

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
poorly means unwell
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk has badly fitted a lamp to the back of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear' belongs to the definition, though it tempts as TAIL in the wordplay; the wordplay begins at 'area'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail light is the red lamp at the back of a car or bike, the light fixed to the rear.

clue.text: Flash limb cycling near Amsterdam on vacation

indicators.note: going round in a loop, so the last letter rotates to the front
a place on vacation is vacated, emptied of everything but its ends
near means next to, so the pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: a leg is a limb
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A showy leg pedals a bike near Amsterdam while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' fits the Dutch scene, but it rotates the letters of the limb. 'Flash' is a noun here, not slang for showy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a brief glint or flicker of light, the same as a momentary flash.

clue.text: Devious raconteur securing obvious power source

indicators.note: devious means not straight, so the letters take a winding route
to secure is to hold fast, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
clear means plain or obvious

explanation.surface: A crafty storyteller grabs an obvious source of influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power source' suggests political clout in the surface but means electricity generation.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor generates electricity from controlled fission, supplying energy to the grid.

clue.text: Fifty diamonds compound stores for UK city

indicators.note: whatever stores goods keeps them inside it

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an ester is a chemical compound
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Fifty diamonds are kept in a warehouse complex for a British city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' suggests a walled enclosure; here it is the chemistry noun. Leicester is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a large city in England's East Midlands, so it fits the label of a British city.

clue.text: Cook made early dinner for busy person?

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or tamper with, so the letters get mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef prepared supper ahead of time for someone with no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the chef in the scene, but it signals mixing up the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A ready meal is a precooked supermarket dish that only needs reheating, handy for people with little time.

clue.text: Cats and pigs barely restrained by locks

indicators.note: barely suggests stripped bare, with the outer layer removed
something restrained is held in, so it goes inside the other piece

blocks.note: tresses are locks of hair
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Cats and pigs are only just kept in by the locks on their pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' is hair, not fastenings, despite the farmyard surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigresses are female tigers, and tigers belong to the cat family, so they are big cats.

clue.text: Shelled food from Spain Mark obtained

blocks.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
a scar is a mark on the skin
got means obtained

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark brought back nuts or seafood from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, but it is a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is the French culinary term for edible snails, served in their shells with garlic butter.

clue.text: Editor inspired by posh relative’s herb rub

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so one piece is drawn inside another

blocks.note: swish means smart and fashionable
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor
MA is a mother, with the possessive S
sage is a culinary herb

explanation.surface: A magazine editor draws ideas from a well-to-do relative's herbal ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'herb rub' reads as a spice mix for meat, but 'rub' alone is the definition. Swish is British slang for posh.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swedish massage is a classic full-body treatment of long kneading strokes, one kind of rubdown.

clue.text: Regard core of protestors gathering from the south

indicators.note: the core is the very centre, so only the middle letters are kept
in a down clue, reading from the bottom upwards runs the letters backwards

blocks.note: the two central letters
a meet is a gathering, as of a hunt

explanation.surface: Look at the hard core of a demonstration massing from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regard' could be a verb meaning look at; it works equally as the noun for respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem and regard both mean respect and admiration held for someone, as nouns or as verbs.

clue.text: Enough specimens unwrapped

indicators.note: taking off the wrapping removes the outer layer, so both end letters go

blocks.note: samples are specimens

explanation.surface: That's enough specimens opened up for testing.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outer S from each end of SAMPLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, more than sufficient, so it covers having enough.

clue.text: Naive having page replacing good clean feathers

indicators.note: replacing means taking the place of, so one letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: green means inexperienced or naive
P is the abbreviation for page
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A gullible page boy replaces good, clean feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: Put P where the G stands in GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds preen by grooming and tidying their plumage with the beak, exactly cleaning their own feathers.

clue.text: Lazy lot around yard becoming high-fliers

indicators.note: to be around something is to surround it, so it sits within

blocks.note: skivers are shirkers who dodge work, a British word
YD is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A bunch of idlers lounging round the yard turn into successful achievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-fliers' suggests ambitious achievers, but is taken literally as people falling from planes. To skive is British slang for shirking.
explanation.definitionFit: Skydivers leap from aircraft at great altitude, so they are literally people flying high.

clue.text: Delay construction in the marketplace

blocks.note: first meaning: to play for time
second meaning: a booth or stand where traders sell goods

explanation.surface: Building work in the town market is being held up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about building delays; it splits into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to stop or put off progress; the noun is a trader's booth set up at a market.

clue.text: PM upset about current form of language

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, and in a down clue that turns the letters upside down
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister is annoyed about the way people currently speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' tempts toward afternoon or a British leader; it is a named Indian Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a characteristic mode of expression of a people or a set phrase whose meaning is not literal.

clue.text: Doctor enraged at pet?

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vet is furious with an animal patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the vet in the scene but is the verb; the question mark marks the answer as one example of a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Great Dane is a huge breed of dog, kept as a household companion animal.

clue.text: Publication Orbiter finally came after you texted

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter only
one thing after another comes behind it in order
in text-message shorthand a word is cut to a single sounding letter

blocks.note: the ISS is the International Space Station, which orbits Earth
U is text-speak for you
the last letter

explanation.surface: The final part of a space probe's message came through after you sent a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orbiter' is the International Space Station, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is one edition of a magazine or newspaper, a single number of a periodical.

clue.text: Mind tips of rare ivy by lake climbing part of plant

indicators.note: the tip of each word is its leading letter

blocks.note: to mind is to look after
the first letter of each word
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Look after the shoots of rare ivy growing beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' looks like a reversal signal in an across clue, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the slender coiling shoot a climbing plant such as a vine uses to grip supports.

clue.text: US LP mum ordered in one payment

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are put into a new sequence

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American record was bought by Mum in a single instalment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' suggests buying the record, but it signals rearranging. An LP is a long-playing vinyl album.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump sum is money paid all at once rather than in instalments, so a single payment.
